com.esignal.jstandard.beans.flex

Interface FlexData

  • All Superinterfaces:
    java.lang.Iterable<java.util.Iterator<FlexDataField>>
    All Known Implementing Classes:
    DbcFlexData, HistoricalBarFlexEvent, HistoricalTickFlexEvent

    public interface FlexData
extends java.lang.Iterable<java.util.Iterator<FlexDataField>>
    The purpose of this class is to hold the Flex related data. Flex data is composed of a schema and binary data (i.e. payload). The schema defines the structure of the Flex payload; the fields that represent the values in the payload. All of the fields defined in the schema represent a record. The payload will contain one or more records.

    The schema defines:

    • all of the fields that make up a record.
    • the order of the fields.
    • the name of each field.
    • the data type of each field.
    • the length of each field.
    Special case handling for variable lengths:
    • when a field has a length defined (i.e. a positive integer), the field's value's length is the same in every record of this payload.
    • a special case is field length of -1. This represents that the field's value is variable length, in each record of the payload.
    • a variable length field's value (in each record of the payload) will be preceded by a stop bit encoded length, which defines the number of bytes of that field's value.
    • a variable length composite type (in each record of the payload) will be preceded by a stop bit encoded length, which defines the number of bytes of that composite field.
    • when the schema has at least one variable length defined (e.g. length is equal to -1), then each record of the payload will be preceded by a stop bit encoded length, defines the number of bytes (i.e. length) of that record.
    • Using the iterator() handles all of this for the client!
    Possible Exceptions:
    • If a protocol error occurs while decoding the payload received in the response, the iterator.next() will throw an InvalidDataException. If this happens, the data received in the response is not reliable.
    • If an incompatible getValueAs...() method is called to read a field value, it will throw InvalidDataConversionException Exception.
    • If iterator() is called on a non-composite type field, it will throw UnsupportedOperationException
    Clients will access Flex Data from a Listener's on*FlexResponse() (e.g. HistoricalTickListener.onTickRecordFlexResponse(HistoricalTickFlexEvent), HistoricalTickListener.onIntradayFlexResponse(HistoricalTickFlexEvent), HistoricalBarListener.onFlexResponse(HistoricalBarFlexEvent) ).

    getRecordCount() can be used to return the number of records in the Flex Data. Use iterator() to iterate the records. Each record is an iterator of FlexDataFields. An alternative to using the iterator (although not recommended), is to use getSchemaType(), getSchema() and getByteBuffer() and process the response yourself.

    Sample code: 

     Iterator<Iterator<FlexDataField>> recordIterator = historicalBarFlexEvent.iterator();
 
 while (recordIterator.hasNext()) {
        try {
                Iterator<FlexDataField> fieldIterator = recordIterator.next();
                while (fieldIterator.hasNext()) {
                        FlexDataField dataField = fieldIterator.next();
                        String fieldName = dataField.getName();
                        FlexData.DATATYPE type = dataField.getType();
                        try {
                                if (FlexData.DATATYPE.COMPOSITE == type) {
                                        // recursively process composite - not shown here (hint: Iterator<FlexDataField> fieldIterator = dataField.iterator())
                                } else {
                                        // process non composite types
                                        Object value = dataField.getValue();
                                        System.out.println(String.format("name: %s type: %s value: %s", fieldName, type, value));
                                }
                        } catch (InvalidDataConversionException e) {
                                //Note: getValue() will use proper type to read the field value and will not throw this exception. 
                                //But if client decides to use getValueAs...() method to read a field value, it will throw InvalidDataConversionException 
                                //for incompatible type. Client can continue reading the flex data received in payload.
                        }
                }
        } catch (InvalidDataException | NoSuchElementException e) {
                // This is a RuntimeException. There is some issue reading the flex data received. The data received in the payload is not reliable.
        }
 }

      • getSchema

        java.lang.String getSchema()
        Returns a String representation of the schema that describes the structure of the Flex payload. This method supports the following FlexData.SCHEMATYPEs:
        • FlexData.SCHEMATYPE.JSON.
        Returns:
        a String representation of the schema for the Flex records.

      • getByteBuffer

        java.nio.ByteBuffer getByteBuffer()
        Returns a ByteBuffer containing a payload of the Flex records. Use getSchema() which describes the structure of the Flex payload. As an alternative, use iterator() to iterate through the records and fields of the Flex payload.
        Returns:
        a ByteBuffer containing payload of the Flexe records.

      • iterator

        java.util.Iterator<java.util.Iterator<FlexDataField>> iterator()
